text: Git branching is a core part of modern version control workflows. Instead of working directly on the main codebase, developers create separate feature branches to build new functions or fix bugs without affecting stable code. Once work is complete, they push the branch to a remote repository and open a pull request. This allows teammates to review changes, discuss improvements, and catch errors before integration. After approval, the branch is merged back into the main branch, often using a merge commit to preserve history. This structured process keeps development organized, reduces conflicts, and ensures the main branch remains deployable at all times.
